title: 2020 Hyundai Creta vs Kia Seltos - Clash of the Korean Cousins | Comparison | Autocar India
description: It's possibly the most important comparison test of 2020 as the new Hyundai Creta takes on its arch rival, the Kia Seltos. We have them both in turbo-petrol DCT guise, but since they're both essentially the same car under the skin, picking a winner is not going to be easy. asr.full_text: There's nothing like a good sibling rivalry, it's always really closely fought and that's what today's battle is going to be as well. These are not identical twins but they do share the same DNA. Yes, I'm talking about the Creta vs Seltos. Now, thanks to Covid, as you can see, we're a little bit delayed and we're doing things differently. Normally, I'd be standing outside and showing you both the cars, but I'm staying in my own car because I've got my mask off adequately, socially distanced and Gavin's in the other car. Since we were out testing cars last, the whole world has completely turned upside down, and I for one, I'm just happy to be behind the wheel once again but let's not waste any more time, let's get right into it. And let me tell you right at the outset that these two cars have a lot in common. They share the same platform, they have the same engines and gearboxes, and even on the inside, a lot of the interior bits are familiar. But what's different is the skin that wraps in all this hardware. So let's take a look at that first. But before we go any further, which would you prefer, the Creta or the Seltos. Let us know down in the comments and if you liked this video give it like. And if you haven't done so already, please subscribe to the Autocar India channel and click the bell icon to stay notified. The Seltos nose also has a lot of styled elements. A split grille, nurled Chrome, smart-looking slim LEDs that stretch its width out and fog lamps that are housed underneath. All across the front there are cuts and curves and lots of definition. The Creta's nose, on the other hand, grabs your attention for entirely different reasons. With its huge cascady grill and uniquely shaped LED headlamps and DRLs. The side profile of both cars is very similar, both, two cars are well proportioned with the big difference being their Alloys and C pillar area. At the rear, like at the front, the Seltos have the classic elements with a lot of intricate details, while the Creta has the more convoluted mishmash of elements. Which ever look you prefer is upto you. But in all these points both I agree the agree Seltaus is the better looking car. When you open up the tailgate, the Creta and Seltaus provide an identical 433L boot space. There is really no visible difference but with the Seltaus's rear seats being little more upright, it does offer that little extra maneuverability for larger bags. But honestly, the difference is too small to even count it as one now let's move to the inside and see how they square up there I really like the design of the cretas dashboard it's clean it's simple and I really like the way the 10.25 inch touchscreen sits flush with the dash making it quite easy to access. I also like this butterfly wing shape for the steering wheel and the big digital dial in the center over there. Now while quality overall is rather good, in some places, particularly right here in front of you on the dash top, you will find some shiny hard plastics and that causes it to lose a premium point to the Seltos. Well the Seltos definitely has softer touch materials, and even the top of the dash plastic is much richer, much better and over all it gives you a richer more premium feel, even the layout of the dash is much nicer and the dials are cleaner, more clearer, the 10.25-inch infotainment is shared and it's the same as the Creta but this one sits up, out of the dash, into a single console that's integrated over the dials as well. Another difference is that the Creta has the wireless charging pad in a more accessible place than the Seltos, which has it tucked in a recess behind the gear lever. In India the back seat of a car can be a deal-maker or a deal-breaker and the Creta clearly has an advantage! It's got the comfier cushioning, the better seat-back angle and better under-thigh support. And as an added advantage you get this massive panoramic sunroof. The Seltos' backseat is also good in isolation, it's spacious and comfortable but in this comparison the seats feel firmer, the under-thigh support is less and the recline angle is a bit more upright. As far as features go, it's 2 pence of this and 5 pence of that. Each car has something that the other one doesn't have. Let's take a look! It's worth noting that the Seltos has recently upgraded its feature list and it's added some features on to each variant to take on the Creta. And, in addition, the GTX and the GTX+, trims now also get all black interiors. However, we had the version prior to the update and while there is a whole list of features that each one has over the other. The key differences of note are that the Creta has the panoramic voice activated roof, the electronic parking brake and paddle shifters which the Seltos does not have. The Seltos on the other hand has over the Creta, a 360-degree camera, front parking sensors in addition to the rear, the blind spot indicator, the heads-up display, rain sensing wipers and the telescopic steering adjust in addition to tilt. Both cars have some quirky bits like the lack of backlight on all buttons except the main window button and both of them have the SOS button that's oddly placed and tends to get activated at times when you adjust the rearview mirror. Now it's important to tell you right at the outset that we have each checked out both these cars extensively earlier on and driven them back to back but in the interest of social distancing, for this shoot, we'll just stick to our individual cars, Both cars in the comparison today, are the 1.4 liter, turbo direct injection petrol engines with the DCT automatic gearboxes, their outputs of 140 horsepower and 242 NM are exactly the same. It's only their ARAI fuel-efficiency ratings that are slightly different, with this Creta having the slight advantage. Now, out on the road the Celtos gets off the line quite aggressively. In fact, the clutch release is quite sharp so it can catch you out in slow-moving traffic or when you're parking on a slope and you give it that little extra bit of gas it tends to lurch forward. So one has to be a little careful with that. But otherwise than that, this engine is refined it feels strong the performance is really enjoyable. However when you compare it to the Creta the kickdowns are a little slower and that shows up in the in gear acceleration times where the Creta is quicker. In the flat out acceleration though the Seltos has a slight advantage and it's probably down to the sharper clutch release that gets it off the line aggressively. The Creta's clutch progression feels a lot smoother compared to the Seltos and overall, it feels like the much nicer gearbox especially at lower speeds. This makes the Creta much better suited to hustling around in traffic. But, if you find yourself in an open-road and want to drive quickly, the Creta has one more distinct advantage, and that's paddle shifters! And the paddle shifters are a real welcome addition, especially on a turbo variant like this, which most people will buy for the fun to drive factor. As far as handling goes, it's the Seltos that gives you that little more confidence the steering feels weightier, there's less body roll and it's just the one that goes around corners better. While most people may not drive their cars enthusiastically on a winding section of road, and this may not make a difference on other variants, we do have to remember that these are the turbo petrols, and the people who buy this variant are also looking for an enjoyable experience behind the wheel. Yes that's right Renuka, because the Creta steering is lighter, which is good for the city but other than that it's not as consistent as the seltos and around the corners the Creta does have a lot more role too. When it comes to ride quality, both cars are very comfortable but the Creta does have a little bit of an advantage. It rounds off bumps significantly better and has an extra layer of absorption that the Seltos simply does not. And this is an advantage that can be felt in the back seat as well. Isolating your passengers from what's going on underneath the wheels. This is so strange! This is a safe distance I think. Well, what do we think, it's really gross isn't it. And well, I guess it would be because really they have so much in common these two cars but I think after driving them extensively... Yeah absolutely, I think once you drive them back to back, you really can tell the difference is between the two. The Seltos, the interiors, just have that slightly more soft touch materials. The dash layout is a little bit nicer and the interior just feels richer. The experience behind the wheel is one that you enjoy more, especially if you enjoy driving. It just feelings more stable, more planted and of course there's those looks that isn't even a contest, I mean there's no debate there. Nope, I have to agree with you there, 100%. I know they were trying to go for something bold with the Creta. A bit to bold I think? A bit too bold, I can't wrap my head around the looks but one thing's for sure, they seem to have learned their lessons from the Seltos in making the Creta, for instance the gearbox is a lot smoother, the ride is just that little bit more comfortable and they have focused more on the back seat which is just that little bit plusher in this car but it still so very close, even the price of these two top-end DCT turbo-petrollers is within Rs10,000 of each other. Splitting hairs Gavin, and I think we have to not be socially distanced but put a paper between these two cars to actually separate them, that's how close the battle is and I don't think we've seen one that's been fought so hard in a long, long time. It is tough to pick a winner and frankly I don't think you would be wrong to buy either one of these cars. The Seltos, those looks, they grab your attention immediately. The interiors feel more premium, like I said and of course that experience behind the wheel. If you are an enthusiast like me, you will definitely enjoy driving this one, yeah. A lot more. But in saying that, I think the Creta has its strengths. It has a few features that really, you know, give it an edge over this like the panoramic sunroof and the paddleshifters, those are really key additions and I think, you know, it balances out that experience behind the wheel and in the back seat much better. So you can enjoy driving the car, but the backseat is definitely more comfortable than the Seltos. So you know if you are choosing a car that is an entire package, then I'd have to say that the Creta edges but edges by the minutest margin ahead. Well, I have to say I agree and for once, I don't think we can shake on it. No...I guess it's just... so long, farewell, good. Goodbye this time.
